text: You're in! I can see everything on your camera. Four niches, one for each department.
Look at the shelves. Broken jars, every one of them. Why break them all?
And look, past the fallen rocks, further down: the great door! An empty circle, cut into four. Something goes in there.
Wait… those rocks weren't there this morning. I walked straight down those steps at dawn. That tremor in the tunnel must have brought them down.
Field Leader, hand out Packet 1. Departments: find out what your niche is hiding.
Wait… what you found isn't only for you.
Every department will find something another department needs.
Look at the paths! Pass your find on, and keep what you get safe. It's for later.
Wait… look at your four finds. There are lines carved on the back of each one!
They fit together… it's a map of this room! And a path… from the Archive niche, all the way around the rocks!
A hidden way. The Keeper built a second way down, only for those who could read the niches.
Archive, press the back of your niche. Gently…
It's opening! A tunnel… going down, around the rocks!
Carefully, everyone. Follow the light. This is the hall of the great door.
A seal is a stamp pressed into clay over a jar. If the seal is unbroken, no one ever opened the jar.
Field Leader, hand out Packet 2. Inside: four pieces of a seal. Only one is real.
Part A uses your packet. Part B uses what another department gave you.
A seal proves that something was never opened. That is the whole point of a seal.
Look for what was kept pure.
One quarter at a time. The circle is filling up!
Part A first, then Part B. That's what Eli always says.
A real seal was pressed into soft clay. Its picture comes out the right way round.
One small jar. One true seal. Look closely.
It's opening… it's opening!
I couldn't move that door this morning. You did it tonight!
Your signal is breaking up… stay close together.
Eight jars… still sealed! Every other jar was broken, but not these.
Only one carries the true seal. Each department holds one real quarter of it.
Hold your quarter against every jar. Call out the jars that don't match.
Hurry, the lantern's getting low!
The Talmud, in tractate Shabbat, tells it: they searched, and found only one jar of oil with the seal of the Kohen Gadol.
Just like they did long ago, in the Holy Temple. Someone made this room so it would never be forgotten.
And inside it, a rolled-up note. It says: Not gold. Light. Signed: the Keeper.
…Light? That's the treasure?
Better than gold, Noa.
Oil for one day. In the Holy Temple, Hashem made it burn for eight. The Talmud tells it, and so does Megillat Antiochus, the Scroll of the Hasmoneans.
Bring the little jar and the Keeper's note out with you. Carefully: the Keeper made them so we would remember.
Look down the hill: the river, and our lantern at base camp on the far side. And there you are, on the hillside!
You carried one little light through all that darkness. A little light pushes away a lot of darkness.
Head down to the old campsite at the foot of the hill and light a fire. We'll cross the river the moment the water drops!
All four niches are open! We've never seen anything like it.
Field Leader, has every department passed on its find?
Got everything? Then back up the tunnel, everyone!
Up the tunnel… and there it is: the way out. Night sky, and the rain is back.
I can see the opening! You're almost out!
Get back! Get back from the rocks!
Expedition? I can see you all. Everyone's safe. But the way out… it's buried under the rocks.
The ground here isn't stable. I'm so sorry. I told you it had settled.
So they're stuck in there?
But wait… this was a hideout. A hideout always has a second, secret way out!
Look, on your camera! A narrow path, going down, on the left!
Take it. Slowly. Follow the light down. We're right here with you.
Your signal is breaking up… we can barely hear you…
If we lose you: Field Leader, you're in charge now. Trust each other. You can do this!
Then: silence. The signal is gone.
We can see your lantern coming down the hill… and now your fire! You made it!
The water's dropping! We're crossing now. Start without us!
We've waited all night to hear this. What did you learn along the way?
Each department, tell us what your puzzle and your Field Notes taught you.
Now the whole story. Think of the little jar, your lantern in the dark, and the Chanukah candles. What do they teach us?
We made it across the river. We're here with you!
I've waited my whole life for a find like this. Thank you.
You were amazing! Can I join your class?
On behalf of the museum: this discovery is yours.
Now come into the tent, everyone. Your Expedition Record is waiting for its stamp.
The wheel turns. Stone grinds on stone… and the secret door swings open.
Cold night air. The rain has finally stopped. Stars… and then…
…Expedition? EXPEDITION! Can you hear me?!
They're out! They're out!! I can see the stars on their camera!
Baruch Hashem. You're safe. You're all safe.
You found the secret exit on your own. Field Leader, you brought them all out. I can breathe again.
And the code on the wheel: twenty-five! Kaf is twenty, Heh is five, like the two letters on the great door!
It's hidden in the name Chanukah: Chanu, “they rested,” and Kah, twenty-five. They rested from the fighting on the twenty-fifth of Kislev!
K-25! The site's name! It was telling us all along!
The two letters on the great door, the ones I couldn't read at dawn! The Keeper hid the date there, so it would never be forgotten.
At the bottom of the path: a second door, locked. In its middle, a stone wheel of symbols and letters.
And on the walls beside it, two carvings.
Base camp can't help you now. Your Field Leader will.
All four quarters! The seal is whole again!
It's very quiet down there… Field Leader, does a department need a clue?
The lantern's flickering! Check every jar!
Judah, called the Maccabee. Archive: show Survey his mark.
Kaf and Heh. Conservation: what are they in Greek numerals?
Click. The wheel holds one code. It waits for the other.
Expedition… two thousand years ago, someone hid one little jar of light, so it would never be forgotten.
Tonight, you found it. And now you are the ones who remember.
Happy Chanukah, everyone! Light your candles where the whole street can see!
Go light up the world.
Wait! Stop! Don't push that one yet!
Slowly, everyone. Hold every quarter against its seal first. All four of them. Then tell your Field Leader what you see.
The whole story, in order, from the decree to the eight days.
That was so fast! Survey, you're naturals.
Another department will need that column. Watch the door.
Seven lamps, straight branches: the Temple Menorah, exactly as described.
Not the Chanukah one with eight!
Conservation, that's careful work. A real conservator's hands.
Al Hanissim: Hashem gave the strong into the hands of the weak, the many into the hands of the few.
Archive, I couldn't have read it better myself.
Another department will need those glyphs. Watch the door.
Yehochanan, the Kohen Gadol: a real coin, over two thousand years old. Beautifully read, Inscriptions.
Most experts think he was a grandson of Matityahu. Matityahu's family were Kohanim who stood up for the Torah.
His family's coin… in this cave? Maybe this was their hideout!
Broken jars, and the oil made impure, just like in the story. Your quarter reads Kohen.
Another quarter in. Well done, Survey.
The vine matches the column exactly!
Conservation, you made that look easy.
Eight days: the time it took to make new pure oil.
That's what the eight notches mean! Archive, you're brilliant.
A stamp in clay reads the right way round. Inscriptions, you found the real one!
Another quarter for the door. I've waited all day for this.
More than two thousand years ago, the Land of Israel was ruled by the Syrian-Greek kingdom.
Their king wanted the Jewish people to forget the Torah. He forbade learning it, and keeping its mitzvot, like Shabbat.
His soldiers entered the Holy Temple in Jerusalem and made it impure, and the lights of the Menorah went dark.
Many were afraid. A few refused to forget the Torah.
Matityahu and his sons left their town, Modiin, and went up into the hills of Judea.
The historian Josephus wrote that they fled to the mountains, and many families followed them, to live in caves.
From these hills they fought the king's army and protected their people. Some say there were secret tunnels too.
Today. The same hills.
Last night: the worst storm in a hundred years.
For hours the rain poured down these slopes, and the ground grew heavy… and soft.
Then, with a roar, part of the hillside gave way!
And behind the mud, where no one had looked for two thousand years: a doorway, cut into the rock.
I'm Dr. Tamar Lev. At dawn I went in alone.
Deeper in: a room cut into the rock, with four empty niches. At the back, steps going down… and there, a great stone door.
An empty circle. Eight notches. Two letters I couldn't read.
I pushed. It wouldn't move. Then the radio called me back: the river was rising!
Can you hear me? Oh, good. This is base camp.
The river washed out the road. We're safe, but we can't get back to the site. We call it Site K-25.
Eli Sofer, archivist. I read old words: Torah, Talmud, prayers, and old scrolls like Megillat Antiochus.
I'm Noa! Old maps call that place the treasure room. Maybe there's gold!
We look for the truth, Noa. Carefully.
If the rain comes back, the mud could bury that doorway again. We only have tonight.
We heard your class has been learning about Chanukah. By the Jewish calendar, it happened between the years 3597 and 3622: more than two thousand one hundred and sixty years ago.
And our tests date this cave to that very time. Who could help us better than you?
Your school is on the near side of the river. You're the only ones who can reach it.
So we need you. From this moment, you are the expedition.
Your teacher is the Field Leader, the only one on the radio with us. Bring every answer to the Field Leader.
Field Leader, is every department at its table?
An expedition has departments. Form four groups, two to five explorers each.
Every table has a sign. Find yours, that's your department!
Not sure where you belong? Ask your Field Leader. That's what Field Leaders are for.
On your table is your department's Starter folder. Open it together.
Three rules before you go in.
One. Your Starter folder holds tools only your department has. Keep them safe: other departments will need your help.
Two. Handle every find gently. Cut only on dashed lines.
Three. Found an answer? Bring it to your Field Leader, who radios it to us. Done before the others? Your Field Leader may have a field task for you.
Is everything clear?
Field Leader, take them in. Stay close. Follow the light.
Wait… did the ground just move?!
Expedition? Expedition, can you hear me?!
…there. Signal's back. Old tunnels settle after rain. You're safe. Keep walking.
I can see what you see. Keep going… there.
Come in, come in, out of the cold. Everything you found, right here on our table.
The column. The Menorah. The prayer. The coin. The seal. And the little jar, with the Keeper's note.
And your Expedition Record! Dr. Lev, the stamp!
And one more thing: a certificate for every department. We've all signed them. Your Field Leader will sign them too, and hand them out.
That old box in the corner? Things we found around the site that nobody can explain yet.
Maybe one day you'll help us with those too.
You'd help us with those too? Thank you! That old box has waited a long time for someone like you.
And thank you for helping with our old mysteries tonight. That box finally has some answers!
Survey, your column told the whole story, and your Field Notes say why we keep telling it. What's the lesson?
Conservation, you rebuilt the Temple Menorah. Your Field Notes tell where the light should go. What's the lesson?
Archive, your eight days went from olives to new oil, one day at a time. What's the lesson?
Inscriptions, your coin belonged to the Kohen Gadol's family, and one small jar carried his seal. What's the lesson?
Survey discovery. The Story Column. They tell what happened, from the decrees to eight days of light.
Conservation discovery. The Menorah Blueprint. Just as the Torah describes it, ready to be lit again in the Holy Temple.
Archive discovery. The Prayer of Contrasts. Hah shem gave the few victory over the many.
Inscriptions discovery. The Coin of the Cohen Gadole. Mah tee tyah hoo's family were Kohaneem.
Survey discovery. The Word Cohen. The seal belonged to the Cohen Gadole.
Conservation discovery. The Vine Border. The seal was pressed on one little jar.
Archive discovery. The Eight Days. Until new pure oil could be made.
Inscriptions discovery. Seal or Impression. The real seal piece is found.
The One Sealed Jar. Like the one jar they found in the Holy Temple, the Keeper sealed one jar to remember it.
Match each carving to a sentence in the journal. What happened first?
Both vines must join across every break. If they don't, try another drum.
The bottom drum shows the decrees; the top drum shows the eight days of light.
Count the cups, knobs and flowers on the stem first.
22 − 4 = 18 cups for six branches: how many on each? Do the same for the knobs and the flowers.
Exodus says each branch has three cups, a knob and a flower. Check every strip, carefully.
Find the pairs first: the line must join across the break.
In each pair, who won? Put the winner on the right.
The prayer starts with the strong and the weak.
Use the old-letter chart in your Starter folder.
Read from the right, like Hebrew today. Start with the middle line.
The middle line is הכהן: now find the same letters in the next line.
Plot every jar from the log first.
Pieces found beside opened jars are out.
Read what is left with the Letter Key: the seal belonged to the Kohen.
Rebuild the little jar first and look at the seal's border.
The border goes dot, dash, dot, dash.
Find the little jar drum on the Story Column. Which way does its left vine lean?
Put the day cards in order. How many days are there?
Rule out pieces with the wrong number of notches.
Count the cups on a branch of the Menorah Board.
Compare the old letters with your coin. Are any backwards?
Backwards pieces are seal stones, not impressions.
Read the Contrast Key from top to bottom, then the piece from right to left.
